name: Hamzah Zainudin
_note: M1 dry-run subject: opposition frontbencher, the hardest harmonization case. Scored period is his closed tenure as Leader of the Opposition (Dec 2022 to Apr 2026). Data on file, below ranking validity (peer set < 3 and most governing-centric dimensions are not applicable to an opposition role), so no composite or rank is published. He remains the elected Member for Larut. Layer B (Editorial Panel) added 2026-06-01 as a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

periods.office: Leader of the Opposition, Dewan Rakyat (17th)

metrics.justification: No personal corruption charge or conviction of record against the leader. The graft cases reported in 2024-2025 are against his former political secretary and, separately, his son, not the leader himself. Under the A5 attribution rule an associate's or family member's case is not the leader's status, so it is not recorded against him. Status is therefore 'none-on-record'.

citation.title: Former political secretary to Hamzah Zainudin goes on trial Aug 25 over RM350,000 graft charges

metrics.justification: Shapley-Shubik power index of the leader's bloc (Perikatan Nasional, the main opposition) among the seven blocs of the 222-seat Dewan Rakyat (GE15, simple-majority quota 112), computed by scripts/compute-pivotality.mjs. PN=0.2214 on 74 seats. Pivotality is descriptive structural weight and applies to opposition blocs identically; it is not a merit score.

metrics.justification: As Opposition Leader his institution-building was thin: he personally downgraded a 26-member "shadow cabinet" to an informal "monitoring" committee within days (Feb 2023), and on the Parliamentary Services Bill 2025 (a parliamentary-independence reform his own bloc long sought) PN abstained at the 4 Mar 2025 vote and he sought delay. Diluted/partial reform record (anchor 2).

citation.title: Most Parliament staff disagree with Parliament Services Bill 2025, claims Hamzah

metrics.justification: In Sept 2024 PN under his leadership rejected the government-opposition MOU on equal MP constituency allocations, a cross-bench instrument, citing contested terms, while leaving the door open to resume talks "if terms are fair" (Nov 2024). Declined a cross-bench instrument without eroding norms (anchor 2).

citation.title: Perikatan Nasional unanimously rejects government-opposition MOU

metrics.justification: Reversed a firm "I am staying" stance as Opposition Leader (14 Feb 2026, after his Bersatu sacking) by resigning the post in Apr 2026, citing political stability; the stated reason was publicly contradicted by coalition figures who described other motives. A reversal with a stated but contested explanation (anchor 2).

citation.title: Hamzah resigns as opposition leader, cites political stability
